subject: Error in # read the files to a methylRawList object: myobj

messages.author: 3c464c42d9250881
messages.subject: Error in # read the files to a methylRawList object: myobj
parts:
I have used methylKit several times and have not had a problem loading in my datasets before.  I have a new dataset w/96 individuals.  I parsed the data using an awk command to create the methylation call columns (## chrBase chr base strand coverage freqC freqT).  The coverage columns are all integer and the freq C and freq T are sometimes non-integer numbers.  Every file has a mix of these.  I keep getting errors, just in some of the files when I try to read in the methylRawList object;

The error reads:  Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings,  :
  scan() expected 'an integer', got '5.55556'

When I peruse the file, I will find this particular (or whatever integer throws an error) and 1 or more will be found in the freqC column.  I'm stumped as to why this is a problem, and also why some files read in perfectly fine.  

Any suggestions or thoughts?

Thanks

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Error in # read the files to a methylRawList object: myobj
parts:
The package decides the column classes of the table by reading in first 100 lines. So in some cases, the first 100 will only have integers for freqC and freqT, and those columns will be expected to have integers only. providing the column classes beforehand is essential to read the files fast. So awk way to deal with this would be  to append ".0" to freqC and freqT columns for the rows that do not have a "." already.

For more,  you need to share your sessionInfo() and the subset of the dataset and a script that reproduces the problem. I'm not 100% sure that is the problem but it likely is.

Best,
Altuna
